blocks.title: Enthalpy change of combustion
blocks.text: The standard enthalpy change of combustion of a substance is the enthalpy change involved when one mole of the substance is completely burnt in excess of oxygen, under standard conditions.
It is always exothermic. For example, standard enthalpy of combustion ΔH°C of ethanol is –1368 kJ mol⁻¹.

blocks.text_alt: C₂H₅OH(l) + 3 O₂(g) → 2 CO₂(g) + 3 H₂O(l)    ΔH°C = –1368 kJ mol⁻¹

blocks.text: Enthalpy change of combustion is useful in calculating calorie content of foods and fuels.
